blogs.title: The 1.58- Revolution: How BitNet b1.58 Shrinks 70B Models to Fit on Your Laptop
blogs.description: Discover how the new BitNet b1.58 architecture uses a unique ternary weight system (-1, 0, 1) to slash memory usage by up to 90% and speed up inference significantly. This post breaks down the technical magic that allows a 70-billion parameter model to outperform a standard 3-billion parameter FP16 model, making enterprise-grade AI accessible on consumer hardware.

blogs.title: From Floating Point to Fast Integers: The Secret Sauce of BitNet's Compute Paradigm
blogs.description: Why does training on floating-point numbers slow everything down? We dive into the computational mechanics of BitNet b1.58, explaining how replacing billions of complex floating-point multiplications with simple integer additions drastically reduces energy consumption and latency. Learn why 'less is more' when it comes to the actual math powering your LLMs.

blogs.title: Is Now The Time to Abandon FP16? Scaling Laws in the Era of 1-Bit LLMs
blogs.description: Traditional wisdom says bigger models need more resources, but BitNet b1.58 flips the script entirely. Explore the 'new scaling law' introduced in this research, where smaller, 1-bit models can match or exceed the performance of massive full-precision counterparts. We'll look at real-world benchmarks showing how this changes the economics and environmental impact of running Large Language Models.

blogs.title: AI on Your Phone: Why Edge Computing Just Got a Boost from Ternary Weights
blogs.description: Forget cloud-only AI; imagine powerful LLMs running natively on your smartphone or smartwatch. This post focuses on how BitNet's innovations—specifically its support for smaller model sizes and reduced memory bandwidth—make deploying sophisticated language models on edge devices (CPU/Mobile) not just possible, but practical, paving the way for ultra-private and instant AI experiences.
